narrative.overview:
Harness is a private, permission-based sales assistant for meeting notes and answers grounded in supplied facts. Clarity comes first. The interface is an original compact desktop utility with the restraint of professional tools such as Linear; references guide principles, not copied layouts or branding.

The current foundation supports saved preferences, tray access and shortcuts. Connections extends the same utility language to explicit ChatGPT account selection, browser-based sign-in, and permissioned API fallback settings. The meeting surface adds permissioned local setup, explicit capture states, retained local context, and finalized transcript provenance. Backend integration, live provider acceptance, and Windows-native behavior remain explicit until verified. Normative pins remain Poppins+Geist Mono, no shadows, customicons, noSparkles, and compactdesktop. Current UI verification passes with no shadows, no runtime errors, and no overflow at the 420px Windows minimum width.
keyCharacteristics: Poppins UI and Geist Mono code
Per-meeting consent and retained local transcript
dos: Use shared tokens and original geometric icons.
Preserve accessible focus and reduced motion.
Show actual availability and context provenance.
Make account selection, browser sign-in, provider order, model discovery and fallback consent understandable.
Keep meeting setup, capture state, transcript source/time, and local-save status explicit.
donts: No shadows, Sparkles or serif fonts.
No invented statistics, quotas or live functionality.
Do not copy reference product layouts.
Do not mark OAuth, credential-vault, model-discovery or Windows-native acceptance complete from a preview screenshot alone.
Do not treat meeting-active-fixture.png as actual recording; it is root IPC mock proof only.
Do not claim live capture is proven while native Windows acceptance is pending.
Keep native sending disabled until a meeting and inference selection are available; preview sending remains disabled.
narrative.sessionControls: Session fixture proves explicit discovery/selection, cancellation, failed sign-in recovery, local sign-out feedback and draft preservation at 420px/520px. It is synthetic UI evidence; live OAuth, DPAPI and native Windows acceptance remain unverified.
narrative.streamingResponses: Native question/speech/retry/cancel controls; fresh automatic consent; per-attempt stale protection; GFM and bounded lazy Shiki JS highlighting from existing tokens; safe native web links; no remote images. Response fixtures are synthetic, not Windows runtime proof.
